subject: Evaluation success criteria, acceptance tests, and guardrails — MAP draft
messages:
From: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@acmehealth.io>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: samantha.li@acmehealth.io
Date: 2026-12-11T09:02:00Z
Subject: Trial evaluation — request for MAP + acceptance tests

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo last week. The clinical ops team at Acme Health wants to run a three-week eval of Redwood for our chart summarization pipeline. Before we kick off, they asked for a mutual action plan (MAP) and a clear set of success criteria and acceptance tests they can run from their QA environment. In particular they care about:
- latency at 95th percentile under 50ms for single-record inference (100-200 tokens)
- end-to-end accuracy against our clinician-labeled set (target >= 92% F1 on the summary extract task)
- reproducible audit logs and KV cache retention for 14 days

Can you send a draft MAP that shows owners, dates, and exit/stop gates? Also, what test harnesses would Redwood expect us to run vs. what you will validate on your side?

I attached a short intake doc from our QA team (see attachment).

Thanks,
Alex Ramos
Sr. Product Manager, Acme Health
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@acmehealth.io>, Samantha Li <samantha.li@acmehealth.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-11T15:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Trial evaluation — request for MAP + acceptance tests

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the intake doc. I put together a short MAP draft and an acceptance-test matrix and attached both (redwood-map-draft.xlsx, acceptance-test-matrix.md). High-level summary below so the execs can read quickly:

Summary (one-glance):
- Scope: 3-week trial; two endpoints (summarize_record / extract_med_entities)
- Critical success metrics: 95p latency < 50ms (p95), f1 >= 92% on labeled dataset, audit-log completeness >= 99% (no missing request ids)
- Exit gates (fail-fast): any single-day regression of >5 points F1 or p95 latency > 100ms for >2 hours -> pause and triage
- Acceptance tests: seed dataset runner (you run), stress-run (we run), concordance sweep (joint), audit-log verification (joint)
- Owners: Acme QA owns dataset and initial run; Redwood owns stress harness, baseline benchmark, and instrumentation changes.
- Timeline: Week 0 (kickoff & infra), Week 1 (baseline runs + minor tuning), Week 2 (concordance & stress), Week 3 (handoff + evidence pack).

Two quick clarifications that often come up:
1) For latency SLOs we recommend running tests from your VPC region to match production network conditions — we'll provide an agent and a reproducible runner.
2) For the F1 target we need a shared evaluation harness and allowed pre/post-processing steps listed in the matrix; otherwise results are incomparable.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the dataset owners + a single point person for run scheduling (if that is Samantha, we'll treat her as schedule owner).
- Ben (cc) will scope any procurement/contract checkpoints that impact timeline (e.g., PO + data access).
- I'll schedule a 30-minute walkthrough of the MAP + matrix tomorrow at 10am PT.

If acceptable I will lock the MAP and create the shared folder with the test harness and a HubSpot playbook so we can track evidence.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-map-draft.xlsx (MAP draft workbook)
Attachment: acceptance-test-matrix.md (test matrix and runner instructions)
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@acmehealth.io>, Samantha Li <samantha.li@acmehealth.io>
Date: 2026-12-12T13:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Trial evaluation — request for MAP + acceptance tests

Looping in procurement notes — quick operational items that affect the MAP timeline:

- Procurement & Data Access: Acme needs a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) signed before we enable customer-uploaded clinical datasets in the trial environment. Legal turnaround typically 3–5 business days; if you need a faster path we can enable a synthetic holdback dataset while the DPA is processing.
- PO and billing: Trial credits are available but coverage for extended stress tests above baseline needs pre-approval; I'll flag any chargeable burst days in the MAP.
- Audit evidence pack: we will produce a handoff folder with perf dumps, KV-cache snapshots, and a log index. If Acme requires signed attestations beyond SOC2, please list them now so we scope the evidence tasks.

We should be able to keep to the 3-week timeline provided DPA and dataset access are cleared by Day -1. If the DPA slips we recommend a two-week delay and a focused lightweight trial (reduced sample size) to keep momentum.

Ben Carter
Director, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachment: procurement-checklist.pdf (stub)
From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@acmehealth.io>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@acmehealth.io>
Date: 2026-12-19T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Trial evaluation — request for MAP + acceptance tests

Thanks — confident this is a clear plan. Quick answers:
- I'm the schedule owner for Acme QA (happy to own run windows).
- Legal confirmed they can review the DPA by 2026-12-22; we can do a limited synthetic-run next week to validate instrumentation while DPA is in review.
- For evidence, we will need a signed log-retention statement and the raw audit indexes for compliance review — please include that in the handoff pack.

We'll accept the MAP draft as-is pending the DPA. Alex and I will run the seed dataset next Monday and post results to the shared Drive folder. Olga — please send the 10am PT invite and the runner artifact.

Best,
Samantha Li
Lead QA Engineer, Acme Health
